title: Why Does Organized Sound Make Us Cry?
question: Music has no obvious survival function, yet it reliably produces chills, tears, and euphoria — why would evolution equip us with such a powerful response to patterned air pressure?
summary: A minor chord resolving to a major one can trigger a genuine physiological response — skin tingling, eyes welling. Music has no direct evolutionary payoff like food or safety, which makes the intensity of our emotional response to it one of the more stubborn puzzles in psychology and neuroscience.
